### Problem: postorder of a binary tree {#sec-tv-p1-post}

::: {.p-statement}
Return the postorder of a binary tree: left subtree, right subtree, then the node.

Constraints: up to $100$ nodes.

Source: [LC 145 · Binary Tree Postorder Traversal](https://leetcode.com/problems/binary-tree-postorder-traversal/){.solved difficulty="Easy"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
The node is last because its answer, if it had one, would need both children. The recursive form says that directly. The stack form waits until the right child is the node just emitted. Reversing a root–right–left preorder is the same list: that walk is reverse postorder.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **Recursion.** Left, right, append.
2. **One stack.** The `last` pointer from @sec-tv-iter.
3. **Reverse.** Push left then right, append on pop, reverse at the end. The list is built backwards.

**Invariant.** When a node is appended, both of its subtrees are already in the output, in postorder.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Recursion

::: {.form-next}
The definition. Fine while the height fits in the call stack.
:::


::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
#| label: tv-post
def postorder_rec(root):
    out = []

    def go(u):
        if u is None:
            return
        go(u.left)
        go(u.right)
        out.append(u.val)

    go(root)
    return out
```

##### C++

```cpp
void postorderRec(TreeNode* u, vector<int>& out) {
    if (!u) return;
    postorderRec(u->left, out);
    postorderRec(u->right, out);
    out.push_back(u->val);
}
```

:::

#### One stack

::: {.form-next}
Same emission point, with `last` standing in for "the right subtree just finished".
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("post", "stack")
    assert str(final) == "[7, 8, 4, 5, 1, 9, 6, 2, 0]"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def postorder_iter(root):
    return postorder_stack(root)


def postorder_reversed(root):
    st = [root] if root else []
    out = []
    while st:
        u = st.pop()
        out.append(u.val)
        if u.left:
            st.append(u.left)
        if u.right:
            st.append(u.right)
    out.reverse()
    return out


sample = from_level([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, None, 8, None, None, 6, 7, 9])
assert postorder_rec(sample) == postorder_iter(sample) == postorder_reversed(sample)
assert postorder_rec(tree_b()) == [7, 8, 4, 5, 1, 9, 6, 2, 0]
assert postorder_rec(None) == []
```

##### C++

```cpp
vector<int> postorderIter(TreeNode* root) {
    vector<int> out;
    vector<TreeNode*> st;
    TreeNode* cur = root;
    TreeNode* last = nullptr;
    while (cur || !st.empty()) {
        while (cur) { st.push_back(cur); cur = cur->left; }
        auto top = st.back();
        if (top->right && top->right != last) cur = top->right;
        else { out.push_back(top->val); last = top; st.pop_back(); }
    }
    return out;
}
```

:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
$O(n)$ time. Recursion and the one-stack form use $O(h)$ memory. The reversed preorder stores the whole list, $O(n)$, before reversing it.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- The empty tree is `[]`. One node is a list of that value.
- Compare `last` to the child pointer, not to the value. Equal values are not the same node.
- After emitting, the cursor must be empty. Leaving it on the node walks into a finished child.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- Comparing `last` to the child's value treats two nodes that share a value as the same node. On `[1,1,1]` the right subtree is skipped and the output is `[1,1]`.
- After a node is emitted, `cur` has to stay empty. A cursor left on that node walks its left spine again.
- Reversing a root–left–right preorder produces right–left–root. The reversal that matches postorder pushes left, then right, and reverses at the end.
:::

**Variants.** Preorder is the same stack, with the visit on the pop and no `last` pointer (@sec-tv-iter). A general tree pushes an exit mark before its children, so the node is emitted when that mark comes back. Freeing the nodes belongs at that same emission, once both children are already gone.
